newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firms after heavy refinery buying.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firms after heavy refinery buying.

text.p: NWE gas oil was firmer on Friday in line with a small hike in underlying futures and stronger premiums buoyed by heavy barge demand, traders said.
A heating oil barge for very prompt delivery traded at June IPE +$4.00 a tonne, some $2.00-$3.00 up on recent traded levels.
A major Rotterdam refiner bought at least 60,000 tonnes of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil on the barge market this week.
A trader for the refiner said that a minor operational problems and German end user demand sparked the buying spree.
Others suggested that the refinery had a problem with its desulphurisation unit.
Nevertheless, most traders agreed that the trade at +$4.00 was well above market levels, with the buyer hoping to push up quotes.
Another barge of Antwerp storage material was heard traded at just June IPE +$1.00.
German DIN cargoes were assessed at June IPE +$4.00-$5.00, while FOD was pegged at June +$3.00-$4.00 in a quiet market.
The physical diesel market was valued around June IPE +$10.00-$1.50, with June EN590 paper traded at +$10.00.
IPE June gas oil climbed $1.00 on the day to settle at $173 a tonne, helped by speculation of Rotterdam refinery problems.
